title: Edge telemetry shard rotation and customer deletion reconciliation
creator: Priya Raman
description: Goal: build a robust, low-latency reconciliation layer that ensures customer-initiated deletion requests for console telemetry (SDK events, usage pings, debug traces) are reliably enforced across both edge shards and downstream analytics materializations. This ticket implements: 1) shard rotation scheme for edge telemetry partitions to shrink exposure window for sensitive event identifiers; 2) per-customer deletion tokens and salted-hash scrubbing applied at ingestion and during backfill; 3) a reconciliation worker that replays deletions to streaming buffers and batch stores and produces a cryptographic deletion ledger for compliance audits. Motivation: current pipeline leaves a sizable window where events in edge shards can be retained beyond deletion requests due to shard TTLs and async backfills. Regulators and enterprise customers require demonstrable enforcement and auditable proof of deletion within defined SLAs.
acceptance_criteria: edge collectors rotate shard keys within configured rotation interval and drop raw-identifiers within 30s of rotation completion
ingest path applies salted-hash scrubbing using customer-specific salts stored in KMS; raw identifiers are never written to long-term stores
reconciliation worker processes deletion tokens and emits idempotent delete markers to (a) streaming topic compaction, (b) parquet batch store, and (c) derived dashboards
end-to-end test demonstrating Right-to-Be-Forgotten completes within SLA (48 hours) for 99%% of requests in staging
deletion ledger contains tamper-evident attestations (signed by service key) and is exportable for compliance review
design_notes: Edge shard rotation: use epoched shard keys with staggered TTLs to limit identifier exposure window; rotation controller runs as a leader-elected service to avoid cross-region collisions

Salted-hash approach: derive per-customer salt via KMS-wrapped key; perform HMAC on identifier before any persistent write; keep plaintext identifiers only in ephemeral memory for immediate processing
Reconciliation: worker subscribes to deletion topic (ordered), materializes a cursor, and issues idempotent tombstone writes to compacted Kafka topics and S3 parquet via delete manifests
Audit ledger: ledger entries are JSON lines signed with a service signing key and checkpointed to an immutable store with retention policy aligned to legal requests
Backfill strategy: incremental, windowed backfills that consult the current delete index to avoid reintroducing scrubbed identifiers
rollout_plan: alpha: enable shard rotation in canary region with low-traffic customers; monitor errors and latency for 72 hours
beta: expand to 20% of customers and run reconciliation worker in read-only dry-run mode to compare intended deletions vs observed
GA: enable full deletion writes, expose deletion ledger export in Console, and coordinate customer communications
rollback: if delete SLAs missed or data loss observed, disable rotation controller and pause reconciliation writes; revert to previous ingestion path
testing_plan: unit tests for salted-hash module, including salt rotation and key expiry cases
integration test: simulate customer deletion request and assert compacted topic tombstone and S3 manifest reflect removal
chaos test: kill leader rotation controller during mid-rotation and ensure coordination finish or safe rollback
privacy smoke test: fuzz synthetic identifiers through pipeline and verify no raw identifiers persist in long-term stores
metrics_and_dashboards: deletion_latency_p50/p95/p99 (time from request to materialized deletion)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Salted-hash mismatch after salt rotation could orphan previously scrubbed rows. Mitigation: maintain a salt-rotation map for N rotations and include compatibility mode in reconciliation worker
Risk: Reconciliation writes cause unexpected cascading updates in dashboards. Mitigation: dry-run mode and staging verification, plus migration-safe manifest format
Risk: Performance overhead at edge from HMAC. Mitigation: native optimized crypto libs, CPU pinning on collectors, and batching of HMAC computations
Risk: Compliance auditors require raw snapshots. Mitigation: provide signed attestations and explain technical safeguards; only export raw data under court order following legal process
